summary: The case involved 512 life convicts from Uttar Pradesh seeking premature release under a state policy. The court examined amendments to the policy, particularly the introduction and subsequent removal of an age-60 requirement for eligibility. It held that premature release applications must be assessed based on the policy in force at the time of conviction, citing Article 21 and precedents like State of Haryana v Jagdish. The final policy, amended on 27 May 2022, removed the age bar and clarified tenure requirements for release, distinguishing between general and prohibited categories of offenders. The court emphasized transparent, non-arbitrary implementation to uphold rights under Articles 14 and 21.
legal_provisions_cited: State of Haryana v Jagdish, 2010 SCC 4 216
State of Haryana v Raj Kumar @ Bitu, 2021 SCC 9 292
final_judgment: The cases of the 512 life convicts are to be considered for premature release in accordance with the policy as it stood prior to the 28 July 2021 amendment, ensuring eligibility is determined objectively and without arbitrary discrimination.
